response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte (synthetic), ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30. Note: the prior report text (heart size normal, lungs clear, no device mentioned) does not match the prior image. See Heart below.
TECHNIQUE: Current is AP, labeled supine portable, with low inspiration, mild rotation and adequate exposure. Prior is PA with adequate inspiration and mild rotation. Prior position is not labeled and looks upright (inferred). Projection differs from the prior, and position, inspiration and exposure also differ. Overall comparability is limited (both blind reads: limited).

LOOK AT FIRST:
- Triage: urgency high; page on call: no. Triage notes SpO2 94 percent with shortness of breath, so the time-sensitive lung findings should be reviewed sooner. Possible tubes are unconfirmed. Review in this order:
- F1: Right perihilar and mid-zone hazy reticular opacity, indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Time-sensitive.
- F2: Left perihilar and mid-zone hazy reticular opacity, indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Time-sensitive.
- F3: Right basal hazy opacity with indistinct right hemidiaphragm, indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Time-sensitive.
- F4: Dense left lower zone and retrocardiac opacity with loss of the left hemidiaphragm outline, indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Time-sensitive.
- F9: Possible tube over the trachea and possible tube or external object over the midline upper abdomen. Neither is confirmed and tip positions cannot be assessed. Indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Time-sensitive.
- F7: Enlarged-appearing cardiac silhouette, indeterminate. Not time-sensitive, but listed for early review. Needs measurement by the radiologist.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: CURRENT: Trachea roughly midline as far as rotation allows. A thin vertical linear density projects over the tracheal air column; an endotracheal tube is possible but not confirmed. Low lung volumes. Bilateral hazy and reticular opacity, most marked in the perihilar and mid zones and extending to the lower zones (right F1, left F2). Hazy opacity at the right base with an indistinct right hemidiaphragm (F3). Dense left base and retrocardiac region with the left hemidiaphragm obscured (F4). These four are indeterminate: technique (AP, supine, low volumes) may explain part or all of the difference from the prior. No pleural line seen to suggest pneumothorax, but supine films are insensitive for this. The cardiac device generator hides the lung behind it in the left upper and mid zones. PRIOR: Trachea roughly midline. Lungs well inflated. Markings within normal limits or slightly prominent in the right perihilar and lower zone. No focal consolidation or discrete nodule seen. No pneumothorax seen. The lung behind the generator is hidden.
- Mediastinum / hila: CURRENT: Upper mediastinum looks wide, as expected on an AP supine film; true width cannot be judged. Hila are indistinct and partly hidden by perihilar haze and device leads. PRIOR: Mediastinal contour not widened. Aortic knuckle visible. Hila not clearly enlarged; the right hilum is partly overlapped by the lead coil.
- Pleura: CURRENT: Left costophrenic angle obscured by basal opacity (F5). Right costophrenic region hazy (F6). Layering effusions are possible but cannot be confirmed supine. No visible pleural line. F5 and F6 are indeterminate; only 1 of 2 blind reads reported each, so the reads did not agree. PRIOR: Right costophrenic angle clear. Left angle partly overlapped by the cardiac apex and soft tissue, with no definite blunting.
- Heart: CURRENT: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged, but this is an AP supine low-volume film and size is not reliable. Left heart border is partly indistinct against left lower zone opacity. PRIOR: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on the PA film; cardiothoracic ratio looks above one half and needs measuring by the radiologist. The prior report states heart size normal; this statement is not adopted. The prior image shows a left chest cardiac device generator with transvenous coil-bearing leads that the prior report does not mention; the radiologist should confirm the report text belongs to this prior image. Devices: Left chest cardiac device generator with transvenous leads on both studies, with coil segments over the right paramediastinal region (superior vena cava) and the lower heart (right ventricle) (F8, both reads stable). On the current, a further lead with electrodes projects over the left heart border, possibly a coronary sinus lead. ECG electrodes and wires are present on the current. No gross lead discontinuity seen.
- Bones / soft tissue: CURRENT: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion seen; detail is limited by portable technique and overlying hardware. No soft tissue gas seen. F10: An oval mottled density projects over the right scapular and glenoid region, next to the right shoulder ECG electrode. It may be an electrode pad or other external material; a bone lesion cannot be excluded. Indeterminate. This was found on a focused recheck made with the indication in view, not on the blind read, so there is no two-read agreement. No matching density is seen on the prior, but projection, arm position and hardware differ. No other definite sclerotic or destructive lesion is seen in the visible ribs, spine, clavicles or shoulders. PRIOR: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion. Shoulders and clavicles look intact. No soft tissue gas.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Bilateral perihilar and mid-zone opacity (F1, F2) and bilateral basal opacity with loss of hemidiaphragm outlines (F3, F4) look denser and less distinct than on the prior. Because projection, position and inspiration differ, whether this is a true interval change is indeterminate. Possible tubes over the trachea and upper abdomen (F9) are not seen on the prior; presence and tip position are unconfirmed. ECG electrodes and wires are new. The right shoulder-region mottled density (F10) has no match on the prior and is indeterminate. Pleural effusions (F5, F6): not comparable between supine AP and the prior. Heart size: not comparable between AP supine and PA; no size change is reported.
- Unchanged: Cardiac device generator and coil-bearing leads are in a similar overall layout on both films (F8, stable). Exact lead tip positions cannot be compared between PA and AP supine projections. No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion on either study. Trachea roughly midline on both, as far as rotation allows.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart enlarged since the prior? (Read A, F7) | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine with low volumes. AP projection and low inspiration both enlarge the heart shadow. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT chest if clinically needed.
- Is the bilateral perihilar and basal opacity a true interval change, and is it fluid, infection or atelectasis? (Read A, F1) | Reason: Supine position, low lung volumes and AP projection crowd markings and mimic basal opacity. The pattern on a single frontal portable film does not separate these causes. | Recommend: Correlate with clinical status. Repeat upright film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Are pleural effusions present, and have they changed? (Read A, F5) | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and shows as haze, not a meniscus. The prior looks upright. The left costophrenic angle is obscured on the current. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there collapse or consolidation behind the heart in the left lower zone? (Read A) | Reason: Retrocardiac density on a single frontal low-volume AP film may be normal overlap, a magnified heart or true lung opacity. | Recommend: Lateral view when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Is there an endotracheal tube or enteric tube, and where are the tips? (Read A, F8) | Reason: Thin linear densities over the trachea and upper abdomen overlap device leads, external wires and the spine. The image is compressed and tip positions cannot be confirmed. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with window adjustment. Confirm clinically which tubes are in place. Repeat the film if a tip is not identified.
- Have the cardiac device lead positions changed? (Read A, F8) | Reason: PA versus AP supine projection alters the apparent lead course and tip position. The generator also projects differently. | Recommend: Compare on matched PA and lateral views, with device interrogation if there is clinical concern.
- Is the mediastinum widened, or are the hila enlarged? (Read A) | Reason: AP supine projection widens the mediastinum. Perihilar haze, mild rotation and device leads obscure the hila on the current. | Recommend: Repeat PA film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest if clinically warranted.
- Is there a pneumothorax or free gas under the diaphragm? (Read A) | Reason: Supine films are insensitive for both. Air collects anteriorly and may not produce a visible pleural line or a subdiaphragmatic crescent. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, or CT, if clinically suspected.
- Is there lung disease behind the device generator in the left upper and mid zones? (Read A) | Reason: The generator covers part of the left lung on both films, and covers a different part on each because the projection differs. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Has the heart size changed? (Read B, F7) | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine with low volumes. AP projection and poor inspiration both enlarge the heart shadow. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT if clinically needed.
- Are the bilateral perihilar and basal opacities a real interval change? (Read B, F3) | Reason: The current film is supine, AP and low volume, which crowds the lower zones and makes vessels more prominent. The difference is visible, but technique might explain it. | Recommend: Repeat upright film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest. Correlate with clinical status.
- Are pleural effusions present on the current study? (Read B, F6) | Reason: On a supine film, fluid layers posteriorly and appears as hazy density, not a meniscus. Both costophrenic angles are indistinct on the current film. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a pneumothorax or free subdiaphragmatic gas on the current study? (Read B) | Reason: A supine portable film is insensitive for both. Air collects anteriorly and may not produce a visible pleural line or a crescent under the diaphragm. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, or CT if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a new endotracheal tube, enteric tube or central line, and where are the tips? (Read B, F8) | Reason: Linear densities over the trachea and mediastinum overlap device leads, ECG wires and the spine, and the image resolution is limited. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing and edge enhancement. Confirm against the clinical record of placed devices. Repeat the film if tip position remains unclear.
- Has the mediastinal width or hilar size changed? (Read B) | Reason: Supine AP projection, low volumes and mild rotation widen the mediastinum and distort the hila. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Have the cardiac device leads moved? (Read B, F8) | Reason: The projection, patient position and inspiration all differ, which changes the apparent lead course and tip location. | Recommend: Matched PA and lateral films and device interrogation if there is clinical concern.

IMPRESSION:
1. F1: Right perihilar and mid-zone hazy reticular opacity, more conspicuous than on the prior. Indeterminate; technique may explain part or all of the difference. Time-sensitive.
2. F2: Left perihilar and mid-zone hazy reticular opacity, more conspicuous than on the prior. Indeterminate; same technique limits. Time-sensitive.
3. F3: Right basal hazy opacity with indistinct right hemidiaphragm. Indeterminate. Time-sensitive.
4. F4: Dense left lower zone and retrocardiac opacity with loss of the left hemidiaphragm outline. Indeterminate. Time-sensitive.
5. F9: Possible tube over the trachea and possible tube or external object over the upper abdomen, not on the prior. Unconfirmed; tip positions cannot be assessed on this image. Indeterminate. Time-sensitive.
6. F7: Enlarged-appearing cardiac silhouette on both studies. No size change can be called because the projection differs. The radiologist should measure the cardiothoracic ratio on the PA prior.
7. F5, F6: Possible bilateral pleural effusions, left costophrenic angle obscured and right costophrenic region hazy. Indeterminate and not comparable; only 1 of 2 blind reads reported each. Pneumothorax and free gas cannot be excluded on a supine film.
8. F10: Indeterminate mottled density over the right scapular and glenoid region that may be an external electrode pad; a bone lesion cannot be excluded. Noted in the context of known prostate cancer. Not part of the blind read.
9. F8: Left chest cardiac device generator and leads in a similar overall layout to the prior. Stable. Lead tip positions cannot be compared across projections.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Repeat upright PA and lateral chest radiograph with good inspiration when the patient is able, to reassess the lung opacities, heart size, mediastinum, retrocardiac region and pleura.
- CT chest if clinically warranted. No interval is specified in the findings.
- Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest for possible pleural effusions and for pneumothorax or free gas if clinically suspected.
- Review the source image in PACS with window adjustment, including bone windowing over the right shoulder region (F10). Confirm clinically which tubes are in place. Repeat the film if a tube tip is not identified.
- Radiologist to measure the cardiothoracic ratio on the PA prior and confirm that the prior report text belongs to the prior image.
- Matched PA and lateral films, with device interrogation if there is clinical concern, for the cardiac device leads.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
